newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Navy agrees to sell base to Orlando, Fla..
newsitem.headline: U.S. Navy agrees to sell base to Orlando, Fla..

text.p: The U.S. Navy signed an agreement to sell the 1,100-acre Orlando Naval Training Center to City of Orlando, Fla., for at least $1.2 million, The Orlando Sentinel reported Tuesday.
Deputy Undersecretary of Defense John Goodman announced the signing of the deal Monday in San Antonio, Texas, during a conference for communities that have bases slated for closure.
The deal is scheduled for completion by April 15, 1998. The city will take possession of most of the base in 1998, with the remainder coming in 1999 after the base's nuclear power school closes.
The city plans to sell the land to housing developers, who will raze the barracks and classrooms and build offices, parks, schools and more than 3,000 homes and apartments.
In addition to the $1.2 million sale price, the Navy will receive a percentage of the city's profits from the resale of the land.
The city will begin seeking bids from developers in December and award the bids early next year.
